title: Conversation titles and About summaries describe only the latest request, not what's still in context
body:
## Problem

In a long conversation, the AI-generated title and the About summary describe only the most recent request. They should describe everything that is still in the conversation's context.

Example: conversation 2878 is a weeks-long orchestration session. Its Claude Code transcript is `~/.claude/projects/-home-eltmon-Projects-overdeck/0974944a-eba1-43b8-9888-a2a123b5047f.jsonl` (30,328 lines, about 83 MB). The periodic AI refine renamed it "Overdeck intro video revisions and deployment". That was only its last topic.

## Evidence (conversation 2878)

Claude Code compacted this session four times. Each compaction wrote a `system`/`compact_boundary` record, followed four lines later by a summary record:

| compact_boundary line | summary line | summary length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6508 | 6512 | 13,122 chars |
| 12363 | 12367 | 13,201 chars |
| 18930 | 18934 | 13,905 chars |
| 25040 | 25044 | 14,506 chars |

Each summary record looks like this:

```json
{"type":"user","isCompactSummary":true,"isVisibleInTranscriptOnly":true,
 "message":{"role":"user","content":"This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.\n\nSummary:\n1. Primary Request and Intent: ..."}}
```

`message.content` is one plain string. Every summary opens with "1. Primary Request and Intent", which is exactly what a title needs. These summaries are the model's own account of what is still in context. Overdeck's own compaction writes the same shape (`src/dashboard/server/services/conversation-compaction.ts:78`, `:156-157`), so one fix covers both.

## Root cause

The compaction summaries never reach the title or About prompt. They are dropped by the parser, before any windowing happens.

1. **The parser drops the summary.** `src/dashboard/server/services/conversation/parser.ts:204` (string content) and `:264` (array content) pass user text through `renderableUserText`. That calls `isSystemInjection` in `src/dashboard/server/services/conversation/message-filters.ts:8-14`. Line 11 returns `true` for text starting with "This session is being continued from a previous conversation", so the message is not added to `messages`. Hiding it from the chat view is correct. The side effect is that the summary is also missing from everything that serializes `messages` for a model.
2. **The parser keeps no summary text.** It sees the boundary at `parser.ts:474-486` but stores only `{id, timestamp, trigger, preTokens, model}` in `compactBoundaries`.
3. **The serializer keeps only the two ends.** For non-specialist conversations `getCachedMessages(sessionFile, false)` (`src/lib/overdeck/conversation-reads.ts:252`) parses the whole file from byte 0. `serializeConversationTranscript` (`src/lib/conversations/transcript-summary.ts:72-93`) caps each message at `PER_MESSAGE_LIMIT` 1,800 chars. Over `TRANSCRIPT_BUDGET` 24,000 it keeps the first `HEAD_BUDGET` 8,000 chars and the last `TAIL_BUDGET` 15,000 chars (`:37-43`). For title generation, `titleTranscriptWindow` (`:171-179`) narrows this again to 2,500 head + 5,000 tail chars (`:45-47`). In 2878 the model sees the opening turns from weeks ago plus the last few turns, and nothing in between.
4. **The title prompt favors the tail.** `summarizeTranscriptTitle` (`transcript-summary.ts:359-366`) tells the model: "write a 3-8 word title that captures what it is *currently* about. If the topic shifted, favor the most recent direction." (line 362).
5. **The fallback title uses the latest request.** `fallbackTranscriptTitle` (`:114-130`) picks the last `User:` line (`:125`).
6. **The About summary uses the same transcript.** `summarizeTranscriptAbout` (`:372-386`) gets the same head+tail transcript. Its prompt asks for the whole conversation, but it cannot see the middle.

Callers:
- Periodic auto refine: `src/lib/overdeck/title-refinement.ts:88-98` (`handleTurnComplete`, writes `title_source 'ai-refined'`).
- Explicit retitle: `src/lib/overdeck/conversation-reads.ts:787-802` (`retitleConversation`, uses the fallback on timeout).
- About drawer: `src/lib/overdeck/conversation-reads.ts:839-850` (`getConversationAbout`).

## Proposed design

1. **Record the latest compaction summary in the parser.** In the Claude Code parser's user branch, when `entry.isCompactSummary === true`, save `{ text, sequence, uuid, timestamp }` on the parse result as `latestCompactSummary`. Check the flag, not the text prefix. Keep `messages` unchanged so the chat view still hides the summary. The incremental-merge branch in `getCachedMessages` (the `parsed = { ... }` block after `conversation-reads.ts:283`) must carry the field forward: the newer summary wins, and the cached one is kept otherwise. `sequence` already continues across incremental parses (`parser.ts:152`, `:651`), so it can mark where the summary sits. `smart-compaction.ts:253-273` (`findPreviousCompactBoundary`) already reads summary text from raw entries and shows the pattern. Capturing the summary in the parser avoids a second read of an 83 MB file.
2. **Build a context-aware transcript for title and About.** Add a serializer input, for example `serializeConversationTranscript(messages, { compactSummary })`:
   - When a summary exists, put it first under its own label (for example `Summary of earlier context:`). It is not subject to `PER_MESSAGE_LIMIT`, but it has its own cap. Then apply today's per-message cap and tail window to the messages whose `sequence` is after the summary. Skip everything before it, because the summary replaces it.
   - About: keep up to about 14,000 chars of summary, then fill the rest of `TRANSCRIPT_BUDGET` with the most recent turns after the summary.
   - Title: the summary alone (13-14k chars) is almost twice `TITLE_TRANSCRIPT_BUDGET` (8,000). Keep the first ~4,000 chars of the summary (its "Primary Request and Intent" section) plus ~3,500 chars of the latest turns.
   - When there is no summary, keep today's head+tail behavior unchanged.
3. **Change the title prompt.** Replace "If the topic shifted, favor the most recent direction" with an instruction to name the overall scope of the work still in context. The summary covers the earlier work and the recent turns show where it stands. Ask for a title that covers the main thread, not only the newest request. Make the matching change in the About prompt so it treats the summary as the earlier part of the conversation.
4. **Keep the fallback title consistent.** When a summary exists, `fallbackTranscriptTitle` should build the title from the first item of the summary's "Primary Request and Intent" section, not from the last user line. It falls back to today's rule otherwise.
5. **Pass it through the callers.** `title-refinement.ts`, `retitleConversation` and `getConversationAbout` pass `latestCompactSummary` from the parse result to the serializer.

### Other harnesses (fall back to today's behavior)

- **Codex:** rollouts contain `type: "compacted"` records, but `payload.message` is empty. The summary is an `encrypted_content` item of type `compaction` inside `replacement_history`, so there is no readable text. The retained user messages in `replacement_history` are plain text. `codex-conversation-parser.ts` does not handle `compacted` records. Use the fallback.
- **OpenCode:** runs through the ACP parser, which returns `compactBoundaries: []`. The local `opencode.db` has no compaction parts and no summary messages. Use the fallback.
- **Pi:** `pi-conversation-parser.ts:188-193` records compaction boundaries only. Whether Pi's compaction entry carries summary text has not been checked. It can be a follow-up.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parser test: a synthetic Claude Code JSONL with early turns, a `compact_boundary`, an `isCompactSummary` user record, and later turns. `latestCompactSummary.text` is the full summary, and `messages` still does not contain it. An incremental parse that appends a second summary replaces the first. An incremental parse with no new summary keeps the first.
- [ ] `src/lib/conversations/__tests__/transcript-summary.test.ts`: with a compaction summary longer than 1,800 chars plus later turns, the serialized About transcript and the title window both contain the summary's "Primary Request and Intent" text. They contain the turns after the summary and none of the turns before it. With no summary, the output is byte-identical to today's.
- [ ] `tests/unit/lib/overdeck/title-refinement.test.ts`: with an injected `getCachedMessages` returning a summary and later turns, the transcript passed to `summarizeTranscriptTitle` includes the summary text. This proves the summary reaches the model prompt.
- [ ] The title prompt no longer contains "favor the most recent direction". It asks for the overall scope still in context.
- [ ] `fallbackTranscriptTitle` derives from the summary's primary request when a summary is present.
- [ ] Existing tests in these files stay green. `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass.
- [ ] Manual check: re-running retitle and About on conversation 2878 gives a title and summary that cover the orchestration work, not only the intro video.

## Docs to update

- `docs/MODEL-CALLS.md:57-59` (`conversationTitles`, `titleRefinement`, `conversationAbout` rows): describe the new input. The line refs there are already stale (`transcript-summary.ts:31/:230/:235`; the current lines are `:34/:353/:372`).
- `docs/overdeck-remodel/services/conversations.md` (retitle and about rows) if it describes what the model sees.
- The header comment of `src/lib/conversations/transcript-summary.ts` and the `serializeConversationTranscript` doc comment.
